questions.question: What was the most significant geopolitical transformation in North America resulting from the Treaty of Paris of 1763?
options: France ceded all of its mainland North American territorial claims east of the Mississippi River to Great Britain
Spain surrendered all of its Caribbean and South American holdings to the British Empire
The British crown granted complete independence and sovereign neutrality to the Iroquois Confederacy
The American colonies were granted direct representation in the British House of Commons
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the French and Indian War (Seven Years' War). France was virtually driven from the mainland of North America, ceding Canada and all lands east of the Mississippi to Great Britain, and Louisiana west of the Mississippi to Spain.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.2 The Seven Years' War (The French and Indian War)

questions.question:
“And we do hereby strictly forbid, on Pain of our Displeasure, all our loving Subjects from making any Purchases or Settlements whatever, or taking Possession of any of the Lands above reserved, without our especial leave and licence...”
— King George III, Royal Proclamation of 1763

The British crown issued the proclamation excerpted above primarily to:
options: Prevent costly and violent clashes between westward-moving colonial settlers and Native American tribes (such as Pontiac's War)
Reserve the Ohio River Valley exclusively for French Roman Catholic fur-trading corporations
Punish Massachusetts merchants for smuggling molasses into Boston harbor
Force colonists to relocate into industrial manufacturing centers along the Atlantic seaboard
questions.explanation: Following Pontiac's Rebellion in 1763, the British government sought to stabilize the western frontier and avoid expensive military engagements by barring colonists from settling west of the Appalachian Mountains, deeply angering land speculators and frontier farmers.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.3 Taxation Without Representation

questions.question: Colonial opposition to the Stamp Act of 1765 focused primarily on which constitutional principle?
options: Parliament had no legitimate constitutional authority to impose internal taxes on colonies that had no actual direct representation in Westminster
The crown had no authority to collect external duties regulating transatlantic maritime commerce
Colonial assemblies possessed the legal power to veto imperial declarations of foreign war
All taxation violated the English common law tradition and the Magna Carta
questions.explanation: Colonists distinguished between external taxes (mercantilist tariffs to regulate imperial trade) and internal taxes (like the Stamp Act, levying taxes directly on internal paper transactions). Led by figures like Patrick Henry and the Stamp Act Congress, they argued 'No taxation without representation.'
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.3 Taxation Without Representation

questions.question:
“A government of our own is our natural right: And when a man reflects on the precariousness of human affairs, he will become convinced, that it is infinitely wiser and safer, to form a constitution of our own in a cool deliberate manner... than to trust such an interesting event to time and chance.”
— Thomas Paine, Common Sense, January 1776

Thomas Paine's pamphlet Common Sense was uniquely influential in the colonies because it:
options: Used plain, accessible language and biblical allegories to persuade ordinary colonists that complete independence from monarchy was both rational and inevitable
Proposed a compromise restoring colonial dominion under a reformed British Board of Trade
Argued that the colonies should seek military integration into the Spanish Empire
Advocated for the establishment of an American hereditary aristocracy
questions.explanation: Paine avoided dense Latinate legal prose and spoke plainly to the common farmer and artisan. He attacked the institution of hereditary monarchy itself (calling George III the 'Royal Brute of Great Britain') and made a compelling moral and practical case for immediate American independence.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.4 Philosophical Foundations of the American Revolution

questions.question: The Battle of Saratoga (1777) is widely regarded by historians as the turning point of the American Revolutionary War because it:
options: Convinced the French monarchy to enter into a formal diplomatic and military alliance with the United States
Forced the immediate British surrender of their primary naval base at New York Harbor
Led to the immediate capture and trial of British General Lord Cornwallis
Caused the British Parliament to unilaterally repeal the Declaration of Independence
questions.explanation: American victory over General Burgoyne at Saratoga demonstrated that the Continental Army could defeat a major British force in open field combat. This gave Benjamin Franklin the diplomatic leverage needed to negotiate the Franco-American Alliance of 1778, securing French naval, financial, and troops support.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.5 The American Revolution

questions.question: Which of the following events most directly convinced national political leaders such as Alexander Hamilton and James Madison that the Articles of Confederation needed urgent constitutional revision?
options: Shays' Rebellion (1786–1787) in western Massachusetts, which exposed the central government's inability to maintain domestic order or levy taxes
The Whiskey Rebellion in western Pennsylvania against federal excise taxes
The Hartford Convention's declaration opposing the War of 1812
The Nullification Crisis in South Carolina over federal protective tariffs
questions.explanation: Shays' Rebellion—an armed revolt of debt-ridden Massachusetts farmers shut down courts to prevent farm foreclosures—showed that the Confederation Congress lacked the authority to maintain an army or assist states during domestic insurrection, spurring calls for the 1787 Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.7 The Articles of Confederation

questions.question: The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 was one of the most enduring legislative achievements of the Confederation Congress because it:
options: Established a structured pathway for newly settled territories to enter the Union as equal states and prohibited slavery in the Northwest Territory
Allowed individual states to annex western lands without federal approval
Permanently recognized indigenous territorial sovereignty across the entire Ohio Valley
Granted women the right to vote in all newly organized territorial elections
questions.explanation: The Northwest Ordinance established that territories would transition through stages of self-government until achieving statehood on an equal footing with existing states. Crucially, Article VI prohibited slavery north of the Ohio River, establishing an important precedent for federal regulation of slavery in territories.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.7 The Articles of Confederation

questions.question: At the Constitutional Convention of 1787, the Connecticut (Great) Compromise resolved the bitter impasse between large and small population states by creating:
options: A bicameral national legislature with equal state representation in the Senate and population-proportional representation in the House of Representatives
A single executive chosen directly by a popular majority vote across all states
A unicameral legislature where each state delegation possessed exactly one collective vote
A system in which state supreme courts held the power of judicial review over federal laws
questions.explanation: Roger Sherman's Connecticut Compromise blended the Virginia Plan (proportional representation favored by populous states) and the New Jersey Plan (equal representation favored by small states), establishing a bicameral Congress consisting of the Senate (2 senators per state) and the House of Representatives (based on population).
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.8 The Constitutional Convention and Debates over Ratification

questions.question:
“Among the numerous advantages promised by a well constructed Union, none deserves to be more accurately developed than its tendency to break and control the violence of faction... Extend the sphere, and you take in a greater variety of parties and interests; you make it less probable that a majority of the whole will have a common motive to invade the rights of other citizens...”
— James Madison, The Federalist No. 10, 1787

In the excerpt, Madison refutes which classical political assumption held by Anti-Federalists?
options: The belief that stable republican liberty could only survive within small, homogeneous geographic polities
The belief that a powerful standing army was essential for defending civil liberties
The idea that checks and balances between branches were unnecessary in a republic
The belief that pure direct democracy was preferable to representative government
questions.explanation: Anti-Federalists, drawing on Montesquieu, argued that republics could only endure in small, culturally homogeneous societies. In Federalist No. 10, Madison brilliantly turned this on its head, arguing that an 'extended republic' with numerous competing factions prevented any single majority faction from tyrannizing the minority.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.8 The Constitutional Convention and Debates over Ratification

questions.question:
“The great rule of conduct for us in regard to foreign nations is in extending our commercial relations to have with them as little political connection as possible... It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.”
— George Washington, Farewell Address, 1796

President Washington's advice in the excerpt was primarily motivated by his desire to:
options: Protect the young, economically vulnerable United States from becoming entangled in destructive European conflicts between Britain and revolutionary France
Encourage the immediate territorial conquest of Spanish Florida and British Canada
Prevent American merchants from conducting commercial trade across the Atlantic Ocean
Force the United States to join the Holy Alliance of European monarchies
questions.explanation: Washington issued his 1793 Proclamation of Neutrality and reiterated in his 1796 Farewell Address that the fragile American republic needed decades of peace to consolidate its institutions, economy, and military before becoming drawn into European wars.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.10 Shaping a New Republic

questions.question: The constitutional debate between Alexander Hamilton and Thomas Jefferson over the creation of the First Bank of the United States in 1791 centered on:
options: Whether Congress could exercise implied powers under the 'necessary and proper' clause, or whether it was strictly limited to enumerated powers
Whether the federal capital should be moved permanently to Philadelphia or New York
Whether individual states possessed the authority to print their own international gold currency
Whether the Supreme Court had the constitutional power to appoint Treasury cabinet secretaries
questions.explanation: Jefferson argued for 'strict construction'—the Constitution did not explicitly grant Congress power to charter a bank. Hamilton argued for 'loose construction'—the 'elastic clause' (Article I, Section 8) gave Congress implied powers to establish a bank to carry out enumerated fiscal duties (tax collection, borrowing, defense).
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.10 Shaping a New Republic

questions.question: The Virginia and Kentucky Resolutions of 1798, authored secretly by James Madison and Thomas Jefferson, asserted that:
options: Individual states had entered into a compact to form the Union and possessed the authority to nullify federal laws deemed unconstitutional
The President possessed emergency wartime authority to suspend the writ of habeas corpus indefinitely
The Supreme Court had sole jurisdiction to determine the constitutional boundaries of free speech
Immigrants from European nations should be permanently barred from naturalized citizenship
questions.explanation: Passed in response to the Federalist Alien and Sedition Acts, the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions articulated the 'compact theory' of the Constitution, arguing that states formed the federal government and had the inherent right to judge and nullify unconstitutional federal overreach—a doctrine later invoked by Southern secessionists.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 3: Topic 3.11 Developing an American Identity

questions.question: The landmark Supreme Court ruling in Marbury v. Madison (1803), written by Chief Justice John Marshall, was foundational to the American constitutional order because it established:
options: The principle of judicial review, establishing the Supreme Court's authority to declare acts of Congress unconstitutional
The absolute supremacy of state legislation over federal judicial mandates
The doctrine of executive privilege during congressional investigations
The right of the President to remove federal judges without Senate confirmation
questions.explanation: Chief Justice John Marshall struck down Section 13 of the Judiciary Act of 1789 as unconstitutional, establishing that the Supreme Court possesses the definitive authority to review legislative acts and nullify statutes that conflict with the U.S. Constitution (judicial review).
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.2 The Rise of Political Parties and the Era of Jefferson

questions.question: President Thomas Jefferson experienced significant personal philosophical conflict regarding the Louisiana Purchase (1803) because:
options: As a strict constructionist, he recognized that the Constitution did not explicitly grant the executive the power to purchase foreign territory
He believed the purchase would permanently impoverish American agricultural exports
He was committed to an alliance with Great Britain against Napoleonic France
He believed the Rocky Mountains were uninhabitable by agrarian republican farmers
questions.explanation: Jefferson had consistently advocated for strict interpretation of the Constitution, which contained no specific clause authorizing treaties to buy land from foreign nations. However, recognizing the enormous strategic and economic benefits of securing New Orleans and doubling the size of the nation, he pragmatically utilized the presidential treaty-making power.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.2 The Rise of Political Parties and the Era of Jefferson

questions.question:
“The American continents, by the free and independent condition which they have assumed and maintain, are henceforth not to be considered as subjects for future colonization by any European powers...”
— President James Monroe, Annual Message to Congress, December 1823

The Monroe Doctrine declared which of the following core foreign policy positions?
options: The Western Hemisphere was closed to future European colonization, and European intervention in independent American nations would be viewed as an act of hostility
The United States pledged to militarily assist European monarchies in reconquering former South American colonies
The United States claimed imperial sovereignty over all Latin American nations
The United States would unilaterally annex Cuba and Central America
questions.explanation: Drafted largely by Secretary of State John Quincy Adams, the Monroe Doctrine warned European powers against establishing new colonies or attempting to reassert control over newly independent Latin American republics, in exchange for American non-interference in existing European colonies and wars.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.4 America on the World Stage

questions.question: Which of the following technological and infrastructural developments contributed most directly to the Market Revolution of the early nineteenth century?
options: The construction of internal canals (such as the Erie Canal), steamboats, and early railroads linking western agricultural markets to eastern urban centers
The widespread introduction of steam-powered combine harvesters across the Great Plains
The laying of the transatlantic telegraph cable connecting New York directly to London
The federal government's total nationalization of interstate turnpikes and river navigation
questions.explanation: The Market Revolution transformed the US economy from local subsistence farming into a national commercial market network. The opening of the Erie Canal (1825), Robert Fulton's steamboat, turnpikes, and early railroads drastically slashed transportation freight costs, connecting Midwestern farms to northeastern cities.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.5 Market Revolution: Industrialization

questions.question: Under the terms of the Missouri Compromise of 1820, orchestrated by Henry Clay:
options: Missouri was admitted as a slave state, Maine was admitted as a free state, and slavery was prohibited in the Louisiana Territory north of latitude 36°30'
Slavery was banned in all territories acquired from Mexico
Popular sovereignty was established to determine slavery in all western territories
A national referendum was scheduled to decide the emancipation of enslaved laborers
questions.explanation: To preserve the delicate 11-to-11 Senate balance between free and slave states, Henry Clay crafted the Missouri Compromise: Maine entered as a free state, Missouri as a slave state, and all remaining Louisiana Purchase territory north of 36°30' north latitude was closed to slavery.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.3 Politics and Regional Interests

questions.question: How did President Andrew Jackson respond to Chief Justice John Marshall's Supreme Court ruling in Worcester v. Georgia (1832), which recognized Cherokee sovereignty over their ancestral lands?
options: He refused to enforce the Supreme Court decision, facilitating the state of Georgia's dispossession of the Cherokee and the subsequent 'Trail of Tears'
He deployed federal troops to Georgia to arrest state officials who violated Cherokee rights
He negotiated an amendment to the U.S. Constitution granting Native Americans full citizenship
He petitioned Congress to impeach Chief Justice John Marshall for judicial overreach
questions.explanation: In Worcester v. Georgia (1832), Marshall ruled that Georgia state laws had no force on sovereign Cherokee lands. Andrew Jackson famously disregarded the ruling ('John Marshall has made his decision; now let him enforce it'), paving the way for the forced removal of thousands of Cherokee along the Trail of Tears (1838–1839).
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.8 Jackson and Federal Power

questions.question: The Second Great Awakening sparked numerous social reform movements in the 1830s and 1840s primarily through its theological emphasis on:
options: Moral perfectionism and the individual duty to actively eradicate societal sins, including alcohol abuse and human enslavement
Strict Calvinist predestination that discouraged human attempts to reform social institutions
The unquestioned subordination of women to male religious and legal authorities
The separation of moral principles from civic and political participation
questions.explanation: Evangelical leaders like Charles Grandison Finney preached free will and moral perfectionism—the idea that individuals could achieve salvation and had a moral obligation to purge society of vices. This inspired an explosion of antebellum reform crusades: temperance, abolitionism, public asylum reform (Dorothea Dix), and women's rights.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening

questions.question:
“We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all men and women are created equal; that they are endowed by their Creator with certain inalienable rights; that among these are life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness...”
— Declaration of Sentiments, Seneca Falls Convention, 1848

The authors of the Declaration of Sentiments intentionally modeled their manifesto on the Declaration of Independence in order to:
options: Highlight the stark contradiction between foundational American democratic ideals and the widespread legal disenfranchisement and subjugation of women
Propose the immediate secession of northern women from the federal union
Demand the establishment of a female monarchy to govern the United States
Argue that women should abandon civic engagement to focus entirely on the domestic sphere
questions.explanation: Organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott in 1848, the Seneca Falls Convention used Jefferson's iconic prose to expose American hypocrisy: women paid taxes and obeyed laws yet were denied voting rights, property ownership upon marriage (coverture), and access to higher education and professions.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 4: Topic 4.11 An Expanding Democracy & Women's Rights
